item.title: Guardians of accountability: Accounting professionals' roles in fraud prevention and early internal detection
item.content:encoded:
Domenico Campa, International University of Monaco

Dan-Richard Knudsen, NHH Norwegian School of Economics

Aziza Laguecir, EDHEC Business School

Accounting scandals persist despite regulatory reforms and enhanced audit scrutiny, indicating that fraud prevention requires deeper understanding of professional, organisational, and institutional conditions. This special issue addresses an under-researched area: how fraudulent practices can be prevented rather than merely investigated after disclosure, with particular attention to the roles of auditors, certified fraud examiners, and internal accountants as whistle-blowers.

The issue examines how organisational structures, institutional cultures, regulatory environments, and ethical climates influence fraud detection and prevention. It also considers emerging technologies such as blockchain and AI, which create both new fraud risks and detection opportunities, while raising questions about data control and algorithmic bias.

The special issue invites theoretical and empirical contributions that examine fraud prevention holistically, moving beyond compliance-focused approaches to explore the social, institutional, and moral dimensions of integrity and ethical decision-making in accounting contexts.

Appel publié par Accounting Forum. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
